headline: The ratings agency S&P Global expects the UAE and Saudi Arabia to add about 2 to 3 gigawatts of data center power by 2030 and to hold most of the Gulf region's capacity.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a named agency's forecast with figures, but a projection, not a result.
importance_line: Gulf governments, power utilities and data center investors are affected, and the region stays small globally at under 2% of new capacity, but this is one agency's forecast and the large Stargate UAE and state-backed Humain projects in Saudi Arabia could change the totals.
summary: Khaleej Times reports that the credit rating agency S&P Global expects the UAE and Saudi Arabia to add about 2 to 3 gigawatts (a gigawatt is a billion watts) of IT power, the electricity drawn by the computing equipment itself, by 2030 and to account for more than 80% of the Gulf region's data center capacity. That is still under 2% of the world's new capacity over 2026 to 2030, about 70% of which is expected from the US and Canada; Khaleej Times adds that larger projects such as the 5-gigawatt Stargate UAE campus could push the totals higher.
notes: An analyst projection, not a result; S&P's report itself was not opened. The same figures appear in a Zawya copy on TradingView (5 Oct 2026). The link is the page without the AMP parameter the pool link carried.
